mn47:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn47:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn47:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is an inquirer who knows (how to gauge) the state of another’s heart, research should be made by him with respect to a Tathāgata in order to recognize or not he is fully enlightened.’
mn47:3.1: ‘Venerable sir, our dhammas are rooted in the Blessed One, they are guided by the Blessed One, they are centred in the Blessed One. It is good that the meaning of these words should occur to the Blessed One. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will remember it.’
mn47:3.2: ‘Then listen, bhikkhus, and heed well what I shall say.’
mn47:4.1: ‘Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is an inquirer who knows (how to gauge) the state of another’s heart, a Tathāgata should be searched with respect to two kinds of dhammas: with respect to dhammas cognizable through the eye and the ear:
mn47:4.2: “Whether in a Tathāgata’s case dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear are found to be defiled, or not?”
mn47:4.3: When he searches, he comes to know:
mn47:4.4: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are defiled are not found in a Tathāgata.”
mn47:5.2: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are defiled are not found in a Tathāgata” — with that he makes a further search thus:
mn47:5.3: “Whether in a Tathāgata’s case dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear are found to be mixed,[^2] or not?”
mn47:5.4: When he searches, he comes to know:
mn47:5.5: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are mixed are not found in a Tathāgata.”
mn47:6.2: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are mixed are not found in a Tathāgata” — with that he makes a further search thus:
mn47:6.3: “Whether in a Tathāgata’s case dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear are found to be cleansed, or not?”
mn47:6.4: When he searches, he comes to know:
mn47:6.5: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are cleansed are found in a Tathāgata.”
mn47:7.2: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are cleansed are found in a Tathāgata” — with that he makes a further search thus:
mn47:7.3: “Has this venerable one long perfected this profitable dhamma, or recently perfected it?”
mn47:7.4: When he searches, he comes to know:
mn47:7.5: “This venerable one has long perfected this profitable dhamma, he has not recently perfected it.”
mn47:8.2: “This venerable one has long perfected this profitable dhamma, he has not recently perfected it” — with that he makes a further search thus:
mn47:8.3: “Has this venerable one acquired renown, has he reached fame? Are certain dangers in this connexion found in him?”
mn47:8.4: For, bhikkhus, as long as a bhikkhu has not acquired renown or reached fame, certain dangers in this connexion are not found in him,
mn47:8.5: but as soon as he has acquired renown and reached fame, they are found.
mn47:8.6: When he searches, he comes to know:
mn47:8.7: “This venerable one has acquired renown and reached fame, but certain dangers in this connexion are not found in him.”
mn47:9.2: “This venerable one has acquired renown and reached fame, but certain dangers in this connexion are not found in him” — with that he makes a further search thus:
mn47:9.3: “Is this venerable one fearlessly restrained, and not restrained out of fear,
mn47:9.4: and when he does not indulge in sensual desires is it because he is without lust, because of the exhaustion of lust?”
mn47:9.5: When he searches, he comes to know:
mn47:9.6: “This venerable one is fearlessly restrained, and not restrained out of fear,
mn47:9.7: and his non-indulgence in sensual desires is because he is without lust, because of the exhaustion of lust.”
mn47:10.1: ‘Now if others should ask that bhikkhu:
mn47:10.2: “What is his evidence and what is his inference whereby the venerable one speaks as he does—
mn47:10.3: ‘this venerable one is fearlessly restrained, and not restrained out of fear,
mn47:10.4: and his non-indulgence in sensual desires is because he is without lust, because of the exhaustion of lust’?”
mn47:10.5: Then, answering rightly, the bhikkhu would answer thus:
mn47:10.6: ‘Whether that venerable one dwells in a sangha or alone, while there may be some who are well behaved there and some who are ill behaved there and some who teach a group there and some who show themselves (concerned about) material things and some who are unsullied by material things, still that venerable one belittles no one for that.
mn47:10.7: And I have heard and learnt this in that Blessed One’s own presence, received in his own presence:
mn47:10.8: ‘I am fearlessly restrained and not restrained out of fear, and that I do not indulge in sensual desires is because I am without lust, because of the exhaustion of lust.’”
mn47:11.1: ‘About that, bhikkhus, a Tathāgata should be questioned further thus:
mn47:11.2: “Whether in a Tathāgata’s case dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear are found to be defiled, or not?”
mn47:11.3: Answering, a Tathāgata would answer thus:
mn47:11.4: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are defiled are not found in a Tathāgata.”
mn47:12.1: “Whether in a Tathāgata’s case dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear are found to be mixed, or not?”
mn47:12.2: Answering, a Tathāgata would answer thus:
mn47:12.3: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are mixed are not found in a Tathāgata.”
mn47:13.1: “Whether in a Tathāgata’s case dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear are found to be cleansed, or not?”
mn47:13.2: Answering, a Tathāgata would answer thus:
mn47:13.3: “Dhammas cognizable through the eye and ear that are cleansed are found in a Tathāgata;
mn47:13.4: while I have that for my sphere and that for my range, I remain aloof from it.”
mn47:14.1: ‘The teacher who speaks thus is fit for a disciple to approach for the sake of hearing the Dhamma.
mn47:14.2: The teacher shows him the Dhamma at each higher (level), at each superior (stage), with the dark and bright counterparts.
mn47:14.3: According as the teacher shows the Dhamma to a bhikkhu in this way, so he, by directly-knowing some dhamma among the dhammas in that Dhamma, reaches (his) goal, and he has confidence in the Teacher thus:
mn47:14.4: ‘The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered on the good way.’
mn47:15.1: ‘Now if others should ask that bhikkhu:
mn47:15.2: “What is his evidence and what is his inference that the venerable one speaks as he does—
mn47:15.3: ‘the Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered on the good way’?”
mn47:15.4: Then, answering rightly, the bhikkhu would answer thus:
mn47:15.5: ‘Here, friends, I approached that Blessed One for the sake of hearing the Dhamma.
mn47:15.6: The Teacher showed me the Dhamma at each higher (level), at each superior (stage), with the dark and bright counterparts.
mn47:15.7: According as he did so, I came to direct-knowledge here and now of a certain dhamma among the dhammas in that Dhamma, and I reached (my) goal, and I had confidence in the Teacher thus:
mn47:15.8: ‘The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Sangha has entered on the good way.’”
mn47:16.1: ‘Bhikkhus, when someone’s faith in a Tathāgata has by these evidences, these terms and phrases been planted, made to take root and established, then his faith is called supported by evidence, rooted in vision,
mn47:16.2: sound, and invincible by monk or divine or Māra or Divinity or anyone in the world.
mn47:16.3: That is how research with respect to a Tathāgata is according to the Dhamma,
mn47:16.4: and that is how a Tathāgata is well sought in accordance with the Dhamma.’
mn47:16.5: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn47:16.6: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
